# Linear model

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results=FALSE, output=FALSE}
#Load library so functions run smoothly
library(tidyverse)
```

![](images/abundance.png){style="width:200px; background:white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px" fig-align="center"}

MaAsLin3 carries out linear modelling for abundance testing.


## Simple linear regression

A simple linear regression can be carried otu with two variables. These variables are:

- The independent variable: Not dependent on any other variable
    - Preferably controlled by the experimenter
- The dependant variable: Dependant on the independent variable

The below linear regression equation then allows you to predict the value of y when you have the value of x or vice verse.

$$
y = mx + c
$$

Where:

- $y$ = Y variable (dependant variable)
- $m$ = slope coefficient
- $x$ = X variable (independent variable)
- $c$ = intercept coefficient (i.e. y position when x = 0)

An example of a simple linear regression on a chart can be seen below:

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results=FALSE}
#Calculate linear model
petal_width_length_lm <- lm(Petal.Length ~ Petal.Width, data = iris)
#Intercept and gradient
c <- petal_width_length_lm$coefficients[1]
m <- petal_width_length_lm$coefficients[2]
#equation
lm_equation <- stringr::str_c(
    "y = ", as.character(round(m, digits=2)),"x + ",as.character(round(c,digits=2))
)
#plot
iris |>
    ggplot2::ggplot(aes(x=Petal.Width, y=Petal.Length)) +
    ggplot2::geom_smooth(method='lm', formula=y~x) +
    ggplot2::geom_point() +
    ggplot2::annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 6, label = lm_equation) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Petal width", y = "Petal length")
```

## E.coli example

As another example lets look at those treated for an _E.coli_ infection.
In our MaAsLin3 analysis the linear equation may use the abundance of _E.coli_ (post treatment) on the y axis and the antibiotic dosage (mg/kg) on the x axis like so:

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results=FALSE}
set.seed(222)
Dosage <- c(sample(10:100,25), sample(100:500,25), sample(500:1000,25), 
            sample(10:100,25), sample(100:750,25), sample(500:1000,25))
Ecoli <- c(sample(75:150,25), sample(80:180,25), sample(100:250,25), 
            sample(50:100,25), sample(20:80,25), sample(1:40,25))
Ecoli <- Ecoli/10
#AMR shows if AMR was found in Ecoli (AMR) or not (no_AMR)
AMR <- c(rep(x = "AMR", times = 75), rep(x = "no_AMR", times = 75))
#Tibble
tbl <- tibble::tibble(Dosage, Ecoli, AMR)
set.seed(NULL)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results=FALSE}
AMR_tbl <- tbl |> dplyr::filter(AMR=="no_AMR")
#linear rgession
#Calculate linear model
ecoli_lm <- lm(Ecoli ~ Dosage, data = AMR_tbl)
#Intercept and gradient
c <- ecoli_lm$coefficients[1]
m <- ecoli_lm$coefficients[2]
#equation
lm_equation <- stringr::str_c(
    "y = ", as.character(round(m, digits=2)),"x + ",as.character(round(c,digits=2))
)
#plot
AMR_tbl |>
    ggplot2::ggplot(aes(x=Dosage, y=Ecoli)) +
    ggplot2::geom_smooth(method='lm', formula=y~x) +
    ggplot2::geom_point() +
    ggplot2::annotate("text", x = 750, y = 9, label = lm_equation) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Antibiotic dosage (mg/kg)", y = "E.coli relative abundance (%)")
```
